title: src/mixer.rs: weigh the models' predictions by what each has been worth, in the context at hand, instead of averaging them
context: Make the mixer learn. Today Mixer::mix averages the models' stretched predictions, every model counting the same, and Mixer::update learns nothing. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least half a percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes: the message 3,544,012 (one order-2 model, 2.84 bits a character) and the program 1,346,472, of which about 1.3 MB is the frame around it, which you cannot touch. A mixer's code is small; its gain is paid in full once more models are in. Work in src/mixer.rs (new, mix, update). The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.
